stem: The vapour density of a gas is 11.2. The volume occupied by 11.2 g of the gas at STP will be
solution:
Molar mass \(= 2 \times \text{vapour density} = 2 \times 11.2 = 22.4\,\text{g}\,\text{mol}^{-1}\).
Moles in \(11.2\,\text{g} = \dfrac{11.2}{22.4} = 0.5\,\text{mol}\).
Volume at STP \(= 0.5 \times 22.4 = 11.2\,\text{L}\).
Matches option A.

subtopic: SI Units, Physical Properties and Atomic Abundance
stem: The specific heat of a metal is 0.16 its approximate atomic weight would be
solution:
By Dulong and Petit's rule, atomic weight \(\times\) specific heat \(\approx 6.4\,\text{cal}\,\text{mol}^{-1}\,^\circ\text{C}^{-1}\).
Approximate atomic weight \(= \dfrac{6.4}{0.16} = 40\).
Matches option C.

stem: Caffeine has a molecular weight of 194. If it contains 28.9% by mass of nitrogen, number of atoms of nitrogen in one molecule of caffeine is
solution:
Mass of nitrogen in one mole of caffeine \(= 0.289 \times 194 = 56.07\,\text{g}\).
Number of nitrogen atoms per molecule \(= \dfrac{56.07}{14} = 4.00\).
Matches option A.

stem: Volume of a gas at STP is \(1.12 \times 10^{-7}\) cc. Calculate the number of molecules in it
solution:
\(1.12 \times 10^{-7}\,\text{cc} = 1.12 \times 10^{-7}\,\text{mL} = 1.12 \times 10^{-10}\,\text{L}\).
Moles \(= \dfrac{1.12 \times 10^{-10}}{22.4} = 5 \times 10^{-12}\,\text{mol}\).
Molecules \(= 5 \times 10^{-12} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 3.01 \times 10^{12}\).
Matches option B.

stem: The empirical formula of a compound is \(\text{CH}_2\text{O}\). 0.0835 moles of the compound contains 1.0 g of hydrogen. Molecular formula of the compound is
solution:
\(1.0\,\text{g}\) of hydrogen is \(1.0\,\text{mol}\) of hydrogen ATOMS.
Hydrogen atoms per molecule \(= \dfrac{1.0}{0.0835} = 11.98 \approx 12\).
So the molecular formula carries 12 hydrogen atoms, and since it must be a whole-number multiple of \(\text{CH}_2\text{O}\) we need \(2n = 12\), i.e. \(n = 6\), giving \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\).
Of the four printed formulae only the first carries 12 hydrogen atoms; the others carry 10, 8 and 6.
Matches option A.
reviewNote: PRINTED DEFECT, key unaffected. The chosen option is printed C2H12O6 (confirmed at 20x - the first subscript is an unmistakable 2), which is chemically impossible for two carbons and is not a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula CH2O; the intended formula is plainly C6H12O6. The letter is secure anyway, because the hydrogen count alone decides it: the stem's data give 12 H per molecule and only this option carries 12 H (the others carry 10, 8 and 6), so the digit typo in the carbon subscript cannot move the answer. Note separately that C4H8O8 is also not a multiple of CH2O, so only two of the four options are formally admissible.

stem: How many g of a dibasic acid (Mol. wt. = 200) should be present in 100 ml of its aqueous solution to give decinormal strength
solution:
A dibasic acid furnishes 2 replaceable hydrogens, so equivalent weight \(= \dfrac{200}{2} = 100\,\text{g}\,\text{eq}^{-1}\).
Decinormal means \(N/10 = 0.1\,\text{N}\).
Equivalents required \(= 0.1 \times 0.100 = 0.01\,\text{eq}\).
Mass \(= 0.01 \times 100 = 1\,\text{g}\).
Matches option A.

stem: Which of the following cannot give iodometric titrations
solution:
An iodometric titration needs the species to be an oxidising agent strong enough to liberate iodine from iodide, \(2\text{I}^- \rightarrow \text{I}_2 + 2e^-\).
\(\text{Fe}^{3+}\) is reduced to \(\text{Fe}^{2+}\), \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\) to \(\text{Cu}^{+}\) as insoluble CuI, and \(\text{Ag}^{+}\) to silver, so each of those liberates iodine.
Lead in the \(+2\) state has no accessible lower oxidation state in aqueous solution - reduction to the metal is thermodynamically unfavourable - so it cannot oxidise iodide; with iodide it merely precipitates \(\text{PbI}_2\), which is not a redox change.
Matches option C.

stem: A hydrocarbon contains 86% carbon, 488ml of the hydrocarbon weight 1.68 g at STP. Then the hydrocarbon is an
solution:
The mass percentages fix the empirical formula.
Carbon \(= 86\%\), hydrogen \(= 14\%\).
Mole ratio \(\text{C} : \text{H} = \dfrac{86}{12} : \dfrac{14}{1} = 7.17 : 14 = 1 : 2\), so the empirical formula is \(\text{CH}_2\).
A hydrocarbon of general formula \(\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}\) is an alkene, and indeed every alkene is \(\dfrac{12n}{14n} = 85.7\%\) carbon, matching the stated \(86\%\).
An alkane \(\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}\), an alkyne \(\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n-2}\) and an arene all give different carbon percentages.
Matches option B.
reviewNote: The stem's gas data are internally inconsistent and are not needed. As printed, 488 mL at STP weighing 1.68 g gives M = 1.68 x 22.4 / 0.488 = 77.1 g/mol, which is not a hydrocarbon mass at all. With 448 mL it gives exactly 84 = C6H12, consistent with the 86% carbon; 488 looks to be a digit typo for 448. The key does not depend on the resolution, because the 86% carbon alone fixes the empirical formula as CH2 and hence the alkene family.

stem: 16.8 litre gas containing \(\text{H}_2\) and \(\text{O}_2\) is formed at NTP on electrolysis of water. What should be the weight of electrolysed water
solution:
\(2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2 + \text{O}_2\), so the gases come off in the volume ratio \(\text{H}_2 : \text{O}_2 = 2 : 1\), i.e. 3 parts in all.
One part \(= \dfrac{16.8}{3} = 5.6\,\text{L}\), so \(\text{H}_2 = 11.2\,\text{L}\) and \(\text{O}_2 = 5.6\,\text{L}\).
Moles: \(\text{H}_2 = \dfrac{11.2}{22.4} = 0.5\,\text{mol}\) and \(\text{O}_2 = \dfrac{5.6}{22.4} = 0.25\,\text{mol}\).
Water decomposed \(= \) moles of \(\text{H}_2 = 0.5\,\text{mol} = 0.5 \times 18 = 9\,\text{g}\).
Check by mass: \(0.5 \times 2 + 0.25 \times 32 = 1 + 8 = 9\,\text{g}\), as conservation of mass requires.
Matches option B.

stem: \(6.02 \times 10^{20}\) molecules of urea are present in 100 mL of its solution. The concentration of solution is
solution:
Moles of urea \(= \dfrac{6.02 \times 10^{20}}{6.022 \times 10^{23}} = 1 \times 10^{-3}\,\text{mol}\).
Volume \(= 100\,\text{mL} = 0.1\,\text{L}\).
Molarity \(= \dfrac{1 \times 10^{-3}}{0.1} = 0.01\,\text{M}\).
Matches option D.

stem: A commercially sold cone. HC1 is 35% HC1 by mass. If the density of this commercial acid is 1.46 g/mL, the molarity of this solution is : (Atomic mass : Cl = 35.5 amu, H = 1 amu)
solution:
Take \(1\,\text{L}\) of the acid.
Mass of solution \(= 1000 \times 1.46 = 1460\,\text{g}\).
Mass of HCl \(= 0.35 \times 1460 = 511\,\text{g}\).
Molar mass of HCl \(= 1 + 35.5 = 36.5\,\text{g}\,\text{mol}^{-1}\).
Moles \(= \dfrac{511}{36.5} = 14.0\,\text{mol}\) in \(1\,\text{L}\), so the molarity is \(14.0\,\text{M}\).
Matches option C.

stem: The decomposition of a certain mass of \(\text{CaCO}_3\) gave \(11.2\ \text{dm}^3\) of \(\text{CO}_2\) gas at STP. The mass of KOH required to completely neutralise the gas is
solution:
Moles of \(\text{CO}_2 = \dfrac{11.2}{22.4} = 0.5\,\text{mol}\).
Complete neutralisation gives the normal salt: \(\text{CO}_2 + 2\text{KOH} \rightarrow \text{K}_2\text{CO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}\), so 2 moles of KOH per mole of \(\text{CO}_2\).
Moles of KOH \(= 2 \times 0.5 = 1\,\text{mol}\).
Molar mass of KOH \(= 39 + 16 + 1 = 56\,\text{g}\,\text{mol}^{-1}\), so mass \(= 56\,\text{g}\).
Matches option A.

subtopic: SI Units, Physical Properties and Atomic Abundance
stem: The sum of three values 12.0, 19.034 and 2.0143 is equal to X. The number of significant figures in X is
solution:
In addition the answer keeps as many DECIMAL PLACES as the term with the fewest, and \(12.0\) carries only one.
\(12.0 + 19.034 + 2.0143 = 33.0483\), which must be reported as \(33.0\).
\(33.0\) has three significant figures.
Matches option D.

stem: An organic compound having C, H and O has 13.13% H, 52.14% C and 34.73% O. Its molar mass is 46.068 g. What are its empirical and molecular formulae?
solution:
Divide each percentage by its atomic mass.
\(\text{C} : \dfrac{52.14}{12} = 4.345\); \(\text{H} : \dfrac{13.13}{1} = 13.13\); \(\text{O} : \dfrac{34.73}{16} = 2.171\).
Divide through by the smallest, \(2.171\): \(\text{C} = 2.00\), \(\text{H} = 6.05\), \(\text{O} = 1.00\), so the empirical formula is \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}\).
Empirical formula mass \(= 2(12) + 6(1) + 16 = 46\), and the molar mass is \(46.068\), so \(n = \dfrac{46.068}{46} = 1\).
The molecular formula is therefore also \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}\), i.e. ethanol.
Matches option C.

stem: Calculate the amount of \(\text{CO}_2\) gas produced, when 32 g moles of \(\text{CH}_4\) is burned with sufficient amount of oxygen. (Given, atomic weights of C = 12, O = 16, H = 1)
solution:
\(\text{CH}_4 + 2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\), so 1 mole of methane yields 1 mole of carbon dioxide.
Molar mass of \(\text{CH}_4 = 12 + 4 = 16\,\text{g}\,\text{mol}^{-1}\), so \(32\,\text{g}\) is \(2\,\text{mol}\).
Moles of \(\text{CO}_2 = 2\,\text{mol}\).
Mass \(= 2 \times 44 = 88\,\text{g}\).
Matches option C.
reviewNote: AMBIGUOUS AS PRINTED, already recorded in the transcription note: the page reads '32 g moles of CH4'. Read literally as 32 gram-moles the answer is 32 x 44 = 1408 g, which matches no printed option; read as 32 g (= 2 mol) it is 88 g, which is on the paper. The key is recorded on the 32 g reading, since 'g moles' is a stray-word corruption and only that reading produces a printed answer.

stem: Which of the following has the highest mass?
solution:
Convert each to grams.
Sulphur: \(20\,\text{g}\) as stated.
Carbon dioxide: \(4 \times 44 = 176\,\text{g}\).
Hydrogen atoms: \(\dfrac{12 \times 10^{24}}{6.022 \times 10^{23}} = 19.93\,\text{mol}\), mass \(= 19.93 \times 1 = 19.9\,\text{g}\).
Helium: \(\dfrac{11.2}{22.4} = 0.5\,\text{mol}\), mass \(= 0.5 \times 4 = 2\,\text{g}\).
The largest of \(20\), \(176\), \(19.9\) and \(2\) grams is \(176\,\text{g}\).
Matches option B.

subtopic: SI Units, Physical Properties and Atomic Abundance
stem: Which of the following abbreviation is incorrectly represented below?
solution:
In the SI prefixes, d stands for deci, a factor of \(10^{-1}\), so dm is a decimetre; a decametre (\(10\,\text{m}\)) is written dam.
The other three are correctly given: \(\mu\) is micro, p is pico and m is milli.
Matches option B.

subtopic: SI Units, Physical Properties and Atomic Abundance
stem: How many significant figures are there in the answer of the following calculation? \(0.0325 + 0.0812 + 0.0631\)
solution:
In addition the answer keeps as many DECIMAL PLACES as the term with the fewest; here all three carry four.
\(0.0325 + 0.0812 + 0.0631 = 0.1768\), reported to four decimal places.
Leading zeros are not significant, so \(0.1768\) has four significant figures.
Matches option C.

stem: Given below are two statements. Statement I Molality, mole fraction and mass fraction changes with temperature. Statement II Molarity does not change with temperature. choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
optA: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
optB: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
optC: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
optD: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
solution:
Statement I: molality is moles per kilogram of solvent, and mole fraction and mass fraction are ratios of moles and of masses; none involves a volume, and mass does not change with temperature, so all three are temperature independent. The statement is false.
Statement II: molarity is moles per litre of SOLUTION, and a solution expands on heating, so the same moles occupy a larger volume and the molarity falls. Molarity does change with temperature, so this statement is false too.
Both statements are false.
Matches option D.

stem: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion and other is labelled as Reason. Assertion (A) Equivalent weight of crystalline oxalic acid is 63. Reason (R) The compound oxalic acid has 3 valency.
optA: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
optB: Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A.
optC: A is true but R is false.
optD: A is false but R is true.
solution:
Crystalline oxalic acid is \(\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\), molar mass \(= 90 + 36 = 126\,\text{g}\,\text{mol}^{-1}\).
It is dibasic, so its valency factor is 2 and the equivalent weight \(= \dfrac{126}{2} = 63\). The assertion is true.
The reason states a valency of 3, but oxalic acid has only two replaceable hydrogens - and a valency of 3 would give \(\dfrac{126}{3} = 42\), contradicting the assertion it is meant to explain. The reason is false.
Matches option C.

stem: statement I and II use the given options. Statement I The molarity of a solution obtained by mixing 450 mL of 0.5 M HCl with 350 mL of 2 M HCl is 1.25 M. Statement II Molality, mole fraction and mass fraction does not change with temperature. choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
optA: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
optB: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
optC: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
optD: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
solution:
Statement I: moles of HCl \(= 0.450 \times 0.5 + 0.350 \times 2 = 0.225 + 0.700 = 0.925\,\text{mol}\), in a total volume of \(800\,\text{mL} = 0.800\,\text{L}\).
Molarity \(= \dfrac{0.925}{0.800} = 1.156\,\text{M}\), not the \(1.25\,\text{M}\) claimed, so Statement I is false.
Statement II: molality, mole fraction and mass fraction are all built from masses and moles alone, with no volume term, so none of them varies with temperature. Statement II is true.
Statement I false and Statement II true.
Matches option C.
reviewNote: The stem is truncated in print (it opens mid-sentence at 'statement I and II use the given options'), already recorded in the transcription note; the two statements themselves are complete, so the answer is unaffected. Note that this question's option order is the REVERSE of question 19's, so the two must not be graded off one key even though they look parallel - here the both-false choice is first and the both-true choice last.

stem: Select the correct statements from the following. A. In SI system, mole was introduced as fourth base quantity for the amount of a substance. B. The mole of a substance always contains the same number of entities, no matter what the substance may be. C. The molar mass in grams is numerically equal to atomic/molecular/formula mass in kg. D. In three moles of ethane, the number of hydrogen atoms is 6. E. The term gram molecular mass can not be applied for \(\text{SiO}_2\)
solution:
Test each statement as printed.
A: the mole is the SEVENTH base quantity of the SI, not the fourth - false.
B: a mole of any substance contains \(6.022 \times 10^{23}\) entities whatever the substance - true.
C: the molar mass in grams is numerically equal to the atomic or molecular mass in unified mass units (u), not in kilograms - false.
D: three moles of ethane \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\) hold \(3 \times 6 = 18\) moles of hydrogen atoms, i.e. \(18 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}\) atoms, not 6 - false.
E: silica is a giant covalent network with no discrete molecules, so the term gram molecular mass does not apply to it and gram formula mass is used instead - true.
Only B and E are correct.
Matches option D.
reviewNote: Flagged because one printed statement decides the key and its magnitude may be lost in print. Statement D reads 'the number of hydrogen atoms is 6', which is false (three moles of ethane hold 18 N_A hydrogen atoms) - the transcription note records that the PDF text layer holds nothing further to recover. On that reading the correct set is B and E, the answer keyed here. If the source intended '18 N_A' then D is true and the correct set becomes B, D and E, which is also a printed option - so the key would move. Supporting the reading used: statements A ('fourth') and C ('in kg') are each false as printed too, and if A were also intended true the correct set would be A, B and E, which no option offers. A self-consistent question therefore requires A, C and D all to be false, giving B and E. Worth adjudicating against the source.

stem: An organic compound contains 78% (by wt.) carbon and remaining percentage of hydrogen. The right option for the empirical formula of this compound is [At. wt. of C is 12, H is 1]
solution:
Carbon \(= 78\%\), so hydrogen \(= 100 - 78 = 22\%\).
Mole ratio \(\text{C} : \text{H} = \dfrac{78}{12} : \dfrac{22}{1} = 6.5 : 22\).
Divide by the smaller: \(1 : 3.38\), which rounds to \(1 : 3\), giving \(\text{CH}_3\).
As a check, \(\text{CH}_3\) is \(\dfrac{12}{15} = 80.0\%\) carbon, the nearest of the four to the stated \(78\%\); \(\text{CH}_4\) is \(75.0\%\), \(\text{CH}_2\) is \(85.7\%\) and \(\text{CH}\) is \(92.3\%\).
Matches option C.

stem: Which one of the followings has maximum number of atoms?
optA: 1 g of Mg(s) [Atomic mass of Mg = 24]
optC: 1 g of Li(s) [Atomic mass of Li = 7]
optD: 1 g of Ag(s) [Atomic mass of Ag = 108]
solution:
For a fixed mass of \(1\,\text{g}\) the number of atoms is largest for the smallest atomic mass.
Magnesium: \(\dfrac{1}{24} = 0.0417\,\text{mol}\) of atoms.
Oxygen: \(\dfrac{1}{32} = 0.0313\,\text{mol}\) of \(\text{O}_2\), i.e. \(0.0625\,\text{mol}\) of atoms.
Lithium: \(\dfrac{1}{7} = 0.143\,\text{mol}\) of atoms.
Silver: \(\dfrac{1}{108} = 0.0093\,\text{mol}\) of atoms.
Lithium gives the most, \(0.143\,\text{mol}\), even after the oxygen figure is doubled for its two atoms per molecule.
Matches option C.

stem: In this type of questions, a statement of assertion (A) is followed by a statement of reason (R). Mark the correct choice as: Assertion : 1 mole of azide ion and 1 mole of nitride ion contain same amount of charge. Reason : 1 mole of azide ion contains three times the number of nitrogen atoms present in 1 mole of nitride ion.
optA: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
optB: If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
optC: If assertion is true but reason is false.
optD: If assertion is false but reason is true.
solution:
Azide is \(\text{N}_3^-\), carrying one unit of negative charge per ion, so one mole carries \(1\,\text{F} = 96500\,\text{C}\).
Nitride is \(\text{N}^{3-}\), carrying three units per ion, so one mole carries \(3\,\text{F} = 289500\,\text{C}\).
The charges are in the ratio \(1 : 3\), not equal, so the assertion is false.
The reason is true: azide holds 3 nitrogen atoms per ion against 1 in nitride, so a mole of azide holds three times as many nitrogen atoms.
Matches option D.

stem: In this type of questions, a statement of assertion (A) is followed by a statement of reason (R). Mark the correct choice as: Assertion : One mole of \(\text{SO}_2\) contains double the number of molecules present in one mole of \(\text{O}_2\). Reason : Molecular weight of \(\text{SO}_2\) is double that of \(\text{O}_2\).
optA: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
optB: If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
optC: If assertion is true but reason is false.
optD: If assertion is false but reason is true.
solution:
One mole of ANY substance contains \(6.022 \times 10^{23}\) formula units, so a mole of \(\text{SO}_2\) and a mole of \(\text{O}_2\) contain the same number of molecules, not double. The assertion is false.
The reason is true: \(\text{SO}_2\) has molar mass \(32 + 32 = 64\) against \(32\) for \(\text{O}_2\), exactly double - but that governs the MASS of a mole, never the number of molecules in it.
Matches option D.

subtopic: SI Units, Physical Properties and Atomic Abundance
stem: How many different scientific notations may be written for the result 10500 g?
solution:
Scientific notation writes the value as \(N \times 10^{n}\) with \(1 \le N < 10\), and the number of digits kept in \(N\) records how many figures are significant.
\(10500\,\text{g}\) can be written \(1.05 \times 10^{4}\) (three significant figures), \(1.050 \times 10^{4}\) (four) or \(1.0500 \times 10^{4}\) (five), depending on how precisely the trailing zeros were measured.
That is three distinct forms.
Matches option B.

subtopic: Laws of Chemical Combination and Percentage Composition
stem: Different proportions of oxygen in the various oxides of nitrogen, prove the law of
solution:
Nitrogen and oxygen form several different oxides - \(\text{N}_2\text{O}\), NO, \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_3\), \(\text{NO}_2\), \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\) - and for a fixed mass of nitrogen the masses of oxygen in them stand in a simple whole-number ratio.
That is exactly the statement of the law of multiple proportions.
Constant proportions concerns a single compound, reciprocal proportions needs a third element, and conservation of mass concerns totals before and after a reaction.
Matches option B.

stem: Insulin contains 3.4% sulphur. What will be the minimum molecular weight of insulin?
solution:
A minimum molecular weight follows from assuming the smallest whole number of the element - here one sulphur atom per molecule.
That atom contributes \(32\,\text{g}\) per mole and is \(3.4\%\) of the molar mass.
\(0.034\,M = 32\), so \(M = \dfrac{32}{0.034} = 941.18\).
Matches option C.

subtopic: SI Units, Physical Properties and Atomic Abundance
stem: Choose the correct statements. (A) Weight of a substance is the amount of matter present in it. (B) Mass is the force exerted by gravity on an object. (C) Volume is the amount of space occupied by a substance. (D) Temperatures below \(0^\circ\text{C}\) are possible in Celsius scale, but in Kelvin scale negative temperature is not possible. (E) Precision refers to the closeness of various measurements for the same quantity. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution:
Test each statement.
A: the amount of matter in a body is its MASS, not its weight - false.
B: the force exerted by gravity on an object is its WEIGHT, not its mass - false, the two definitions have been exchanged.
C: volume is indeed the amount of space a substance occupies - true.
D: the Celsius scale runs below zero, while the kelvin scale starts at absolute zero and so admits no negative value - true.
E: precision is indeed the closeness of repeated measurements of the same quantity to one another (accuracy is closeness to the true value) - true.
The correct statements are C, D and E.
Matches option B.
